why.title: The idea
why.text: 23…Bxg4!! offers the bishop on g4. Taking it gives Black an attack worth more than the bishop.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 23…Bxg4 puts the bishop on g4 where it can be taken by the f3 pawn. That's a bishop on offer.

why.title: If White takes the bishop
why.text: 24.fxg4 is met by 24…Nxe4, taking the e4 pawn and threatening …Nxd2, winning the queen for a knight. Then 25…b2 pushes the passed pawn to b2, and 26…Qd7 threatens …Nxg4, winning a pawn. Black is still a pawn down, but the attack is worth more: Black is clearly better (−2.71).

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the bishop alone and play 24.Nc6. Black answers 24…Nxc6, taking the knight on c6. Then 25…Qc7 aims at the h2 pawn, a weak point next to the king. Black ends up a pawn ahead: Black is clearly better (−1.55).

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 23…b2, is clearly weaker (−0.62 against −1.55). White answers 24.Rc2, lining up rook and queen on the 2th rank. That would leave Black a little better.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 29…Rxg4+!! offers the rook on g4. Taking it gives Black the material back and more.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 29…Rxg4+ puts the rook on g4 where it can be taken by the knight on f2. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: If White takes the rook
why.text: 30.Nxg4 is met by 30…Qxg4+, taking the knight on g4 with check. Then 31…Qg2+ gives check, and 32…Nxf3+ gives check. Black ends up a piece and a pawn ahead: Black is winning (−9.81).

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the rook alone and play 30.Kf1. Black answers 30…Nxf3, taking the knight on f3 and threatening …Rg1# and mate. Then 31…Rxe2 takes the bishop on e2, and 32…Qxh6 takes the knight on h6. Black ends up a piece and a pawn ahead: Black is winning (−6.81).

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 29…Nxf3+, is clearly weaker (−4.86 against −6.81). White answers 30.Bxf3, taking the knight on f3. Black would still be winning, but far less than after 29…Rxg4+.

why.title: The idea

why.title: What it does instead

why.title: If White takes the rook
why.text: 32.Rxe2 is met by 32…Qxg4, taking the knight on g4 and threatening …Qg1# and mate. Then 33…Kh7 threatens mate, and 34…Bd4 joins the attack on the king. Black ends up a pawn ahead: Black is winning (−6.73).

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the rook alone and play 32.Nh6+. Black answers 32…Qxh6, taking the knight on h6. Then 34…Nxh2+ gives check, and 35…Bxb2 takes the rook on b2. Black ends up a piece ahead: Black is winning (−6.68).

why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 31…Qxg4, is clearly weaker (−4.72 against −6.68). White answers 32.Bxf3, taking the knight on f3 and threatening Bxg4, winning the queen. Black would still be winning, but far less than after 31…Rxe2.
